source.title: Stationary Points of Shallow Neural Networks with Quadratic Activation Function
source.authors: D. Gamarnik; Eren C. Kızıldağ; Ilias Zadik

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves gradient-descent training results for shallow quadratic-activation teacher-student networks, using empirical and population squared risk rather than classification error on benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test any listed version's specific architecture, dataset, or training condition. Its results concern a different model and loss. The initialization guarantee constructs a starting point below an energy barrier; it is not a result about random initialization, so it is not a separate training-outcome row.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional optimization guarantees for shallow quadratic teacher-student networks. These results do not test any listed version: squared regression risk differs from V1's classification error; V2 specifies ReLU networks and teacher/student width comparisons; V4 concerns signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth. No depth, normalization or stability-threshold comparisons are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors prove convergence to zero empirical or population risk conditional on initialization below an energy barrier. For sufficiently wide networks with randomly generated teacher weights, they construct deterministic scaled-identity initializations that satisfy this condition with high probability. Random teacher weights do not constitute random student initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies shallow quadratic-activation networks in a realizable teacher-student setting with squared risk. Its gradient-descent convergence results require initialization below an energy barrier; it does not test the listed benchmark classification recipes or random initialization for training.
record.method_sensitivity: The convergence guarantees depend on initialization being below the rank-deficient energy barrier; the empirical result also states a step-size condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.6 proves approximate stationarity in polynomial time and convergence to zero empirical squared risk from below a rank-deficient energy barrier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For realizable shallow quadratic networks under the stated sampling assumptions, sufficiently low-risk initialization and a suitably small step size guarantee successful empirical-risk optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.7 proves convergence to zero population squared risk from below the minimum risk of rank-deficient weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Population-risk gradient descent in the stated quadratic teacher-student model converges globally from initialization below the rank-deficient risk barrier.

record.problems: The convergence statements are theoretical and conditional on low-risk initialization; they do not establish the benchmark classification or random-initialization outcomes in the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: Theorem 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 give initialization constructions or risk bounds, not separate gradient-descent training outcomes, so they are not rows.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with quadratic activation
rows.size_stated: one hidden layer of width m; m is not fixed
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 2.6 gives a gradient-descent convergence result for empirical risk from an initialization whose risk is below the stated energy barrier.

conditions.value: i.i.d. centered sub-Gaussian coordinates under Theorem 2.1 assumptions

rows.measure: Empirical squared risk and approximate stationarity
rows.value: Theorem 2.6(b) states gradient descent reaches an ε-approximate stationary point in time poly(ε^-1,d), with empirical risk at most 32εσmin(W*)^-2 d^(4K2+4).
rows.uncertainty: Theorem 2.6 gives a probability bound for the result; the sample bound stated for part (c) is N ≥ d^(18+8K1/3).
rows.note: The result is a theorem for the paper's model and squared-risk objective; it is not a classification-error measurement.
rows.check: The stated approximate-stationarity and empirical-risk guarantees are supported, but measure none of the listed versions. Correct the part (c) sample bound in uncertainty to N ≥ d^(18+8K1/3), rather than d^(18+8K2/3). The network width satisfies m ≥ d.

rows.check: The zero empirical-risk limit is correctly recorded as a conditional theorem, but cannot establish any listed version's effect. Its assumptions include the data and teacher-norm conditions of Theorem 2.6, beyond the abbreviated conditions recorded here.
